report:
Typing in the notes box was laggy because every keystroke re-rendered the whole checklist. I moved the note state into its own footer component, and after that none of the 19 keystrokes produced a slow commit (React commit over 16 ms).

## Cause

The `note` state lived in `ChecklistScreen`, which is the parent of the list. Each keystroke re-rendered the screen and every visible `QuestionRow`. Each row also recomputes `riskLevel()` on every render. That function builds `new RegExp` 200 × 30 times per row, so the re-render was expensive.

## Fix

The change is in `src/screens/ChecklistScreen.tsx`. I added a `NotesField` component that owns `note` and the input ref, and the list footer is now `<NotesField />`. Typing now re-renders only that component. Layout, styles and props are unchanged, and the Done button's blur logic moved with it. `tsc` and `eslint` printed no errors, but I didn't capture their exit codes. I did not test the Done button or any other part of the app after the refactor.

## Before and after

I profiled the same scenario both times on a fresh app launch (dev build, simulator). In each run I scrolled to the bottom, tapped the notes box and typed "hello store manager" (19 keystrokes). The counter read 19 / 500 in both runs.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Slow commits (≥16 ms) | 9, each 157–179 ms (about 1,464 ms total) | 0 (all under 16 ms) |
| `QuestionRow` renders | 162 (9 commits × 18 rows), 1,229 ms | no slow commits, so none of the 157–179 ms row renders seen before |
| Fiber renders captured | 2,979 | 216 |
| JS thread busy time in the profile window | 1,630 ms | 76 ms |
| `new RegExp` time (`regExpConstructor`) | 943 ms | 0 ms |
| `riskLevel` self time | 77 ms | 0 ms |

- **Dev-build caveat:** these are dev-build timings, which the profiler says run roughly 3× slower than production. The ratios matter more than the absolute numbers.
- **After-run detail:** the profiler drops per-commit detail when nothing is slow, so I have no per-component render counts for the after run. That is why the `QuestionRow` entry above is inferred. The fiber-render total, the JS busy time and the absence of `riskLevel` and `RegExp` samples in the CPU profile back it up.
- **Keystroke batching:** in the baseline, the 19 keystrokes coalesced into 9 slow commits because each took about 160 ms. A user typing slower would feel one ~160 ms stall per keystroke.

## Other finding, not fixed

`riskLevel` is wasteful in its own right. The 200-iteration loop is redundant, because `hits / 200 >= 1` is the same as "any keyword matches". It also builds a new regex per keyword per render. Tapping yes or no on a question still re-renders all visible rows, so it still costs time there. That is outside this bug report, so I left it alone. Precompiling the regexes once, or caching the result per title, would remove the cost. I can make that change if you want.

I left Metro running. I stopped the simulator-server, debugger and accessibility services I started for this session. The one remaining ID I passed, `3c6dddc3…`, matched nothing because it is Metro's internal handle.
